file_roles.evidence: The generated metaobject carries a type name no compiler can parse back, "error: no member named '__1' in namespace 'std'" on 'QVector<std::__1::pair<QByteArray,QByteArray>>', which is libc++'s inline namespace spelled out inside a type name. The failing file is generated, '.moc/x86_64/moc_qnetworkreplyhttpimpl_p.cpp:235', and no network file was changed; the only non-test source file the fix touched is the metatype header that builds those type names, so the name-building logic there is what was wrong.

rationale: The build breaks in generated code, 'moc_qnetworkreplyhttpimpl_p.cpp:235:87: error: no member named __1 in namespace std', with follow-on errors "'QByteArray' does not refer to a value" and 'type-id cannot have a name' that are consequences of the same unparsable name. The only non-generated, non-test file the fix changed is src/corelib/kernel/qmetatype.h, which is where a type name is composed, so the bad string is produced in one place at compile time and consumed in another, far from the network class whose signal it describes. Nothing in the pasted output names the gold file.
